title: Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2021
short_title: Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2021

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The government introduced the Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill to support the independent review into parliamentary workplaces led by Sex Discrimination Commissioner Kate Jenkins, excluding Freedom of Information Act access to review documents and delaying Archives Act access for 99 years to encourage individuals to come forward.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2021 is necessary to ensure the Sex Discrimination Commissioner's review remains effective and protects the privacy of staff and survivors, and noted bipartisan and crossbench support for the bill, which aims to make Parliament a safe workplace in response to Brittany Higgins' reported assault and broader cultural issues.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The Greens welcomed the Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2021, arguing it ensures confidentiality for submissions to the Sex Discrimination Commissioner’s inquiry into Parliament House culture and safety, and supported an amendment by the member for Warringah. Senator Larissa Waters was acknowledged for raising the issue and negotiating the amendment.

speeches.speaker: Helen Haines
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the government should have acted sooner on an independent inquiry into parliamentary culture, noting the unsatisfactory Gaetjens review and welcoming Kate Jenkins' review. They also stated the government could have passed earlier bills on a parliamentary standards commissioner and sex discrimination law amendments, and supported confidentiality amendments by the member for Warringah.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Archives and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2021, arguing its amendments—including a 99-year suppression order under the Archives Act—are vital to protect the privacy and trust of staff submitting to the Jenkins review into parliamentary workplaces. They also urged the government to enact all 55 recommendations of the Respect@Work report and noted the protections would apply retrospectively to 5 March.
